Keywords: A Lannister Always Pays His Debts

Variants.Content: The Lannister family is based on Casterly Rock and Lannisport. It claims to have originated from the legend that the resourceful Lann obtained the giant rock from the Casterly family. The red lion on a gold background and "Hear my roar" are the official coat of arms and motto; "Lannister must pay his debts" is not a family motto, but it is more widely known than the motto because of its reputation for wealth, credibility and revenge. The Westerlands' network of mines, ports, knights, and vassals taught Lannister early on to treat money as a language of power: rewards can buy loyalty, debts can prolong influence, and respectability can cover rifts. Outsiders often simplify them into gold and arrogance, but people in the West understand that a lion should not only be feared, but also make many people rely on its account book to make a living.

When the princes of the West looked up to Casterly Rock, they saw not only gold mines and lion flags, but also a way of ruling that rewards loyalty, collects debts, and maintains dignity. Lannister can make vassals rich and noble, and can also make a disgraced family find that roads, engagements, and purses are all closed to him at the same time. The lion's grace and wrath rarely stop at one sentence.

Miners, coiners, and merchants of Lannisport know that gold does not flow from songs. It comes from dark mine tunnels, strict ledgers, ship cabins and countless pairs of hands stained with dust. Lannister must pay his debts. He is a guarantee to his creditors and like an iron door that slowly closes to his debtors.

When outsiders talk about Lannister, they often mention gold first and revenge second. They admire Casterly Rock's wealth and wonder if there is a price behind every gift. The strongest thing about the Golden Lion is not that everyone loves it, but that even if many people hate it, they have to calculate what it takes to offend it.

Entry House Lannister Casterly Rock and the golden lion family of Lannisport originate from the witty Lannis legend.
